messages:
infra-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty incident triggered for service=redwood-db-proxy, symptom=high pg connection failures (pgbouncer). Alerts: 3xx errors rising, db.conn.queueing > 85%

pagerduty: Incident fired: RDW-DBP-0032 -> urgent

marta (oncall): I'm on it, grabbing context. seeing spike in client connections to pgbouncer across all prod pods.

raj (sre): adding context: metrics show `pgbouncer_clients` at 18k (normally 2k). `pg.conn_wait` and `pg.conn_queue` spiking. Redis is also reporting `maxclients` nearing limit on cache layer 2.

kevin (dba): timeline? any deploys in the last 10m?

marta (oncall): no deploys in last 30m. Traffic shows a sudden ramp from a handful of heavy customers. Possible load test or runaway loop.

carlos (plat-eng): Rolling mitigation plan: 1) ack PD, 2) apply connection backoff via edge rate limiter for heavy routes, 3) increase pgbouncer pool on standby hosts, 4) restart one pgbouncer pod to clear stuck clients if needed.

marta (oncall): Acked PD. Assigning pager to raj for infra actions, kevin for DB knobs, sophia to coordinate customer comms.

raj (sre): I'm going to scale up pgbouncer replicas + bump `max_client_connections` on the proxy tier. Doing a staged rollout to avoid thundering herd.

kevin (dba): While raj scales, I'll check Postgres `max_connections` and replica capacity. If pgbouncer increases, we need headroom on PG. Prep step: `SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity;` and `SHOW max_connections;`

marta (oncall): paste logs from the proxy showing connection errors:
```
error: failed to acquire client connection: timeout after 1s
WARN connection_pool: accept queue length=4800
```

raj (sre): scaled pgbouncer from 3->8 replicas in region-prod-eu. Watching metrics. CPU stable, accept queue dropping.

infra-bot: autoscaler event: pgbouncer-replicas increased to 8 (requested by raj).

carlos (plat-eng): Also enabling client-side rate-limit rule for route `/v1/generate` for top offending API keys (temporary throttle 5r/s).

marta (oncall): kevin, any risk bumping pgbouncer clients without increasing PG `max_connections`?

kevin (dba): Good call. PG `max_connections` is 1000, current active connections 820. If pgbouncer pool increases we might hit limit. I'll increase `max_connections` to 2000 on standbys then primary if safe, and notify if any long-term impact. Doing it on replicas first.

kevin (dba): Ran `ALTER SYSTEM SET max_connections = '2000'; SELECT pg_reload_conf();` on replicas. Primary change queued pending maintenance window but immediate reload applied on replicas.

raj (sre): pgbouncer accept queue down from 4800 -> 600 in 4m, now 120. Errors falling. 

marta (oncall): Redis also flagged earlier. Sophia, please check support queues for errors tied to embeddings/lookup failures.

sophia (support): Confirmed ~12 customer errors referencing cache misses hitting fallback code. Triage: error rate for embedding lookups up 6x for last 8m. Messaging affected customers with a brief note "experiencing elevated latency for model lookups, investigating".

marta (oncall): Looks like primary impact area: customers doing high fanout generation + warm cache misses. Severity: P2 -> customer-visible latency and some failed requests. No data loss.

raj (sre): Running short-term patch: enabled prefix KV caching on model-serving tier to reduce duplicate backend calls for repeated tokens. Also enabled `continuous_batching=false` on a subset to reduce simultaneous DB hits from batch flush.

kevin (dba): Monitoring replication lag while increasing connections. Lag steady <200ms. No failover risk currently.

marta (oncall): Pager update: manual mitigations applied (pgbouncer scale + PG knob on replicas + client throttles + caching). Errors down ~92% in 18m. Still watching for residual tail latency.

pagerduty: Incident note updated: "Mitigations: scaled pgbouncer, increased PG max_connections on replicas, enabled temporary client throttles and caching. Impact: elevated latency and some failed requests for embedding/lookup routes."

carlos (plat-eng): I'm going to queue a safer autoscale policy change so we have higher floor for pgbouncer during traffic surges. Will follow up with PR.

raj (sre): Next steps checklist I'm doing now: 
- [x] verify client accept queue below threshold
- [x] ensure pgbouncer replicas healthy
- [x] revert any risky config after stable
- [ ] run load test to validate new autoscale rules (post-incident)

marta (oncall): handoff: I'll be oncall for another 30m then handing to raj for watch. If anything regresses, re-open PD.

sophia (support): sent follow-up to affected customers: short summary and ETA for postmortem. A few asked for incident timeline. I'll collect questions.

kevin (dba): adding DB action items for postmortem: evaluate `pgbouncer` pool sizing, connection pooling parameters, and whether `max_connections` bump requires permanent change or more aggressive pooling.

marta (oncall): marking incident as "under control". Closing PD acknowledgement; will leave the thread open for postmortem notes. Great job team. :thumbsup:

pagerduty: Incident acknowledged by marta (oncall).

infra-bot: Reminder: create incident doc at /incidents/rdw-dbp-0032 and tag eng-oncall, eng-runtime, product.

marta (oncall): creating doc now, attaching metrics snapshots and the temporary playbook steps used. I'll also link to rate-limiter audit and list of impacted customer API keys.

carlos (plat-eng): quick idea for long-term: consider adding per-API-key token bucket with fallback queueing on the edge to prevent single tenants from stomping shared pools. I'll sketch RFC post-incident.

raj (sre): agreed. Also propose synthetic traffic detectors to auto-scale earlier when client fanout patterns appear.

kevin (dba): final check: replica `max_connections` now 2000, primary remains at 1000 until maintenance. Monitor for 2h.

marta (oncall): last update: metrics stable for 12m, support queue quieting, no new errors. handing to raj. If anything changes, PD will fire again. Thanks all.

raj (sre): taking watch.

sophia (support): closing customer comm loop for now; collecting requests for the postmortem.

infra-bot: Note: incident RDW-DBP-0032 moved to status=resolved_by_oncall; resolution_note="scaled proxy + temporary throttles; follow-ups scheduled"

marta (oncall): archived artifacts in incident doc and filed follow-ups: action-items assigned to kevin/carlos/raj.

end of thread.
